subject: Private K8s deployment: tenant affinity matrix, storage tiers, and acceptance criteria
messages:

Subject: Private K8s deployment: tenant affinity matrix, storage tiers, and acceptance criteria

Simon / Lisa —

Thanks again for the intake doc (attached). I sketched a first-pass private deployment plan for the BlueHarbor POC and wanted to capture the cluster-level requirements and acceptance criteria up-front so we can converge quickly. Attached: BH-reqs-20260824.pdf (your doc) and redwood-private-architecture-draft.v1.pdf (our proposal).

High-level recommendations (short):
- Cluster model: single control-plane HA (3 masters) + dedicated node pool families for inference, infra, and batch. Keep control-plane isolated on management network with separate K8s API LB in front.
- Node pools: 3 logical types
  - infra (dedicated): 3-5 x m-type (no GPUs) — logging, monitoring, registry, and control-plane-adjacent services.
  - standard compute: N x c-type (customer workloads) with local NVMe for ephemeral cache (fast-ssd storage class).
  - inference/gpu: M x g-type (A40/A100 equivalent) behind a GPU admission policy and quota; preemptible burst allowed only if you accept degraded performance SLA.
- Storage tiers: local NVMe (fast ephemeral, for KV/prefix cache), networked fast-ssd blockstore (replicated across racks, 3-way) for model artifacts and persistent volumes, and an archive object-store (S3-compatible) for long-term snapshots.
- Networking: Cilium with IP-in-IP disabled, BGP peering at leaf routers for stable pod IPs; 9000 MTU recommended for RDMA/throughput-sensitive use cases. No NAT from workloads to customer internal networks — egress via controlled egress gateways with SNAT where required.
- Security/compliance: integrate KMS/HSM for envelope encryption (we can support customer-managed KMS over VPC), enable Pod Security Admission with baseline policies, and enforce image signing + offline registry for air-gapped mode.

Acceptance and performance tests we propose to run during on-site acceptance:
1) Storage IO: fio write/read on fast-ssd class across 2k/4k/1m sizes; target 99th < 20ms for 4k random read on fast-ssd.
2) API server p95 tail latency under simulated control-plane load: < 200ms for listing 1k pods.
3) Inference throughput smoke: sample model load to verify GPU provisioning and kv-cache warm start latency < 25ms per prefix token for 512-token context.
4) Recovery / failover: simulate node loss (worker + network partition) and validate PodDisruption budgets and PV reattachment within SLA window.

Next steps / ask: please confirm (A) whether BlueHarbor requires air-gapped registry + no outbound image pulls, and (B) a hard upper bound on storage IOPS and retention windows for model artifacts (we used 30 TB / 90-day retention as draft).

I'll route this to Karthik and Marissa for the delivery checklist and to Neha for network gating specifics. Proposed meeting to review: Thu 2026-09-03 10:00 PT — does that work?

Best,
Grace

From: Simon Ward <simon.ward@blueharbor.com>

Subject: Re: Private K8s deployment: tenant affinity matrix, storage tiers, and acceptance criteria

Grace —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. A few clarifications from our side (we tried to keep these concise):
1) Air-gap: yes — we need offline image pull via on-site registry. No direct outbound to public registries.
2) Encryption: all persistent disks must be encrypted with customer KMS keys. HSM-backed signing for images would be preferred but we can start with envelope encryption.
3) Latency SLAs: the 4k random read p99 target of < 20ms is aggressive for our geographically constrained site; p95 < 25ms would be acceptable. We will confirm exact IOPS numbers by Tue.
4) Network: we need egress filtering to a set of FQDNs (for telemetry and metrics exporters). Strict BGP is fine but any recommended changes to MTU will need sign-off from our network ops since they control leaf switch configs.
5) Acceptance tests: can you add a test for cold-start model load (download model artifact into local NVMe and measure first-token latency)? We saw regressions here previously.

Also — procurement asked us to include expected procurement timeline: hardware in 8–10 weeks after PO, and they prefer single vendor SOW language for on-site acceptance.

Can you share a short list of what we should expect to see in the SOW / acceptance criteria?

Simon
Simon Ward
Head of Platform Engineering | BlueHarbor Systems
simon.ward@blueharbor.com

Team —

Simon confirmed air-gap + customer KMS encryption and asked for a cold-start model load test plus revised p95 targets. Action items below (I moved the ask into a short mutual-action list):

Action items (who / what / by when):
- Karthik: update the node-pool sizing table with an explicit 'local NVMe warm cache' policy and add cold-start validation steps for model artifact staging. Also include a fallback plan if NVMe capacity is exhausted (eg. spill to fast-ssd with eviction TTL). Due: 2026-09-02 EOD.
- Marissa: draft SOW language for 'on-site acceptance' including the four acceptance tests (fio IO, API server latency, inference throughput, cold-start model load) and a clear pass/fail matrix (p95/p99 thresholds, remediation window). Include hardware delivery acceptance checkpoint and sign-off template. Due: 2026-09-03 AM.
- Neha: confirm recommended CNI & BGP peering runbook and any leaf-switch MTU pre-reqs. Also produce the egress FQDN allowlist pattern Simon asked for. Due: 2026-09-02 noon.
- Grace: I'll provide the initial test harness (simple k8s job templates + fio profiles + a scripted GPU model load test) and coordinate an acceptance dry-run.

Notes / constraints to include in the SOW:
- Delivery window for hardware verification: 10 business days after rack & cable.
- If customer requires strict air-gap with no telemetry, Redwood will provide an offline telemetry collection bundle delivered at acceptance; remote support will be limited until a secure channel is provisioned.
- KMS/HSM integration will require a client-managed key endpoint in their VPC (we canwork with them on a bridge connector).

Simon is looped on this thread for transparency — we'll need his sign-off on the SOW draft before procurement.

Grace

Quick update —

Marissa shared a rough SOW snippet (see linked HubSpot note). I've included the suggested pass/fail thresholds below so we can be aligned before I send the SOW to Simon & procurement:

Proposed SOW acceptance thresholds (draft):
- Storage IO: fast-ssd class p95 read latency <= 25ms for 4k random; p99 <= 60ms.
- API server: p95 list/watch latency <= 250ms under 1k-object scale tests.
- Cold-start model load: model artifact staged to local NVMe and first-token latency <= 120ms for a 512-token context (measured once models are pulled).
- Inference steady-state: per-request kv-cache warmed 95th <= 30ms across 512 context.
- Failover: 95% of stateful workloads reattach PVs and recover within 180s of node removal (documented remediation steps).

I'm OK with these numbers as a starting point; Neha, please confirm the network gating checklist and whether we should recommend jumbo-frames or leave MTU decisions to customer network ops. Karthik, please publish the node-pool table (sizes for infra/standard/gpu, example taints/tolerations, and eviction policies) and add the NVMe eviction TTL/gc guidance.

If we don't hear objections, I'll convert this into the SOW paragraph and push to the HubSpot deal (BH-2026-114) for Simon/procurement review by EOD 2026-09-02.

Thanks —
Grace
